disposition_reason: Table 6 reports Zn, Cu, Fe, Mn, Cr, Ni, Co, Cd and Pb (mean ± SD and range, mg/100 g wet weight) for 13 sugar, syrup, cocoa and chocolate product types; Cd and Pb were not detected in any product.

study.design: market survey of confectionery products with chemometric classification
study.origin: Polish, European and American origin products (as stated)
study.method: FAAS (air-acetylene, deuterium background correction) after microwave wet digestion with HNO3; P by phosphomolybdate spectrophotometry
study.lod_text: Pb<0.01 mg/100 g w.w., Cd<0.003 mg/100 g w.w., Cr<0.02, Ni<0.02, Co<0.01 mg/100 g w.w. (LD = blank mean + 3SD)
study.qa: CRMs tea NCS DC 73351, cabbage IAEA-359, spinach IAEA-331; recoveries 73.5-103% (Pb in tea CRM 87.5%, Cd in cabbage 91.7%) (Table 2)

unresolved: Methods (p. 251) says Pb, Cd, Cr, Ni and Co were all under the detection limits, yet Table 6 reports quantified Cr, Ni and Co for several products; Cd and Pb are ND for every product. Values recorded as printed.
Table 5 macroelements (Ca, Mg, Na, K, P, mg/100 g w.w.) are not extracted as findings; they are nutrients, not contaminants.
Brand count (49 brands) and per-brand data are not given; collection dates not reported.
Some Cr and Co minima fall below the stated LOD (flagged).
